which was received by him from the third respondent.

4.In reply

, the learned counsel submits that without any prejudice, the petitioner is prepared to deposit a sum of Rs.23,00,000/-, before the Special Court for trial of cases under the Tamil Nadu Protection of Interests of Depositors (TNPID) Act, Madurai, in CC No.18 of 2017.

sentences.text: However, he requests that he may be permitted to deposit the said amount in three instalments.
The learned counsel expresses that the petitioner is not willing to deposit this amount before the respondent police.
5.This Court considered the rival submissions made and also perused the materials placed on record.

6.The case of the petitioner is that this petitioner has received a sum of Rs.23,00,000/- from the third respondent, who is an accused in Crime No.1 of 2015, on the file of the Economic Offences Wing (II) (U), Tirunelveli.
He has received the amount for purchase of lands and he is not aware that the said amount has been collected from the depositors and it is in connection with the crime.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Therefore, he has parted this amount to the land owners for purchase of lands.

Since the petitioner fairly admits the receipt of Rs.23,00,000/- from the third respondent herein and he is also prepared to deposit that amount before the concerned TNPID Court, this writ petition is disposed of with a direction to this petitioner to deposit a sum of Rs.23,00,000/-, to the credit of CC No.18 of 2017, which is pending before the Special Court for trial of cases under the Tamil Nadu Protection of Interests of Depositors (TNPID) Act, Madurai, in three instalments as below:-
 i. Rs.10,00,000/- on or before 31.06.2025
